selector.rationale: Presence of anti-centromere antibodies, Raynaud's phenomenon, and skin thickening are characteristic of Limited Systemic Sclerosis, which best explains the patient's symptoms and laboratory findings without contradiction.

rejected.label: Idiopathic Pulmonary Arterial Hypertension
rejected.why: Although the patient has a history of pulmonary hypertension, the presence of anti-centromere antibodies and other systemic symptoms suggest a more complex autoimmune disorder.

rejected.label: Rheumatoid Arthritis
rejected.why: Negative tests for rheumatoid arthritis and lack of characteristic symptoms make this diagnosis unlikely.

rejected.label: Systemic Lupus Erythematosus
rejected.why: Insufficient evidence of characteristic lupus symptoms, such as malar rash, oral ulcers, or nephritis, and low score make this diagnosis unlikely.
